newsitem.title: USA: PJM seen setting record peak power demand Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: PJM seen setting record peak power demand Tuesday.

text.p: The operator of the power grid in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic states said it will likely see record high electricity demand on its system Tuesday as hot, muggy weather continues to bake the region.

"The weather is expected to be same or a little hotter (Tuesday). We may be exceeding our (record) peak," said a spokesman for PJM, officially called the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnect Pool.
PJM, which serves about 9.1 million customers, said the standing record is 48,660 megawatts (MW), set August 2, 1995.
Along with high humidity, forecasters called for temperatures in PJM to hit the 90s Fahrenheit region-wide, with Washington DC thermometers perhaps hitting 100 degrees.

To handle the load, PJM late Monday issued a "hot weather alert" for today, requesting member utilities in the grid to ask customers to conserve energy during hours of peak demand, the spokesman said.
Peak demand is typically hit in mid- to late afternoon.
"We are asking people to conserve by means such as turning down air conditioners and limiting the use of electric hot water heaters," the spokesman said.
The power pool operator also called for part of its "maximum emergency generation" to be put on line at 1533 EDT this afternoon.
